'''Alan Garen''' was an American geneticist who co-discovered [[suppressor mutation]]s for [[tRNA]]. The Garen lab also showed that certain [[Codons|triplet codons]] (5'-UAG, 5'-UAA, and 5'-UGA) failed to bind amino acids.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Weigert M, Galluci E, Lanka E, Garen A | title = Characteristics of the genetic code in vivo | journal = Cold Spring Harb Symp Quant Biol | volume = 31 | pages=145–150 | year = 1966 | pmid = 4866371 | doi = 10.1101/sqb.1966.031.01.022}}</ref> Thus, the Garen lab and Brenner labs are both credited with discovery of the [[Stop codon|stop codons]] of the [[genetic code]].<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Stretton AO, Kaplan S, Brenner S | title = Nonsense codons | journal = Cold Spring Harb Symp Quant Biol | volume = 31 | pages=173–179 | year = 1966 | pmid = 5237189 | doi = 10.1101/sqb.1966.031.01.025}}</ref>

Garen was a professor at [[Yale University]] between 1963 and 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mbb.yale.edu/news/mbb-bids-farewell-tom-pollard-and-alan-garen|title = MB&B bids farewell to Tom Pollard and Alan Garen &#124; Molecular Biophysics and Biochemistry}}</ref> He was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].
